title: Input-validation tests assert on rejection

facts.note: Test URN kind segment identifies an input-validation test; only these tests are scanned (any such test, existing or new).
bun_tester_discipline_detector finding; requires parsing the test body for rejection signals. Fires only when NO listed rejection signal is present.

fires: A Bun test whose URN has a -VALIDATION- kind segment submits only a well-formed payload and asserts success.
A Bun test with -INPUT- in its URN has no .rejects, toThrow, 400/422, invalid, reject or error expectation.
A Bun test with -VALIDATE- in its URN asserts only on the shape of returned data and contains none of the listed rejection signals.
doesNotFire: A test whose URN has no INPUT / VALIDATION / VALIDATE kind segment.
An input-validation test that asserts toThrow("<specific error>") or a 422 status for the declared malformed input.

given: A Bun test whose URN carries an INPUT, VALIDATION or VALIDATE kind segment
then: It MUST drive the malformed/missing/adversarial input named by the acceptance through the production boundary and assert its rejection (.rejects, toThrow, 400, 422, invalid, reject, or an error expectation) for that specific invalid condition.
prefer: Construct the malformed, missing, boundary or adversarial value the acceptance names.
Send it through the same boundary production receives.
Assert the acceptance-specific rejection: exact error, 400/422 response, rejection or throw.
When accepting the bad input could create or mutate state, also assert the rejected request left that protected side effect absent.
avoid: Testing only a well-formed payload (it proves only that the parser works on good input; a well-formed payload proves nothing about adversarial input).
Triggering some unrelated error and treating any rejection as proof (the detector may not flag this, but it does not witness the declared invalid condition).
Bypassing the production validation boundary with a direct fixture assertion.
why: An input-validation acceptance is about BAD input, which a happy-path test never touches — the same silent-green-gap shape as security-auth. It is grouped with the security family because unvalidated input is the entry point for most of what the security rules defend against.
evidence: The test contains a rejection assertion tied to the declared invalid condition, e.g. `expect(() => parseOrder({ sku: null })).toThrow("INVALID_SKU");` or, over HTTP, `expect(res.status).toBe(422);`.
The case would turn red if validation for the declared bad input were removed.
The observed failure is caused by the intended validation rule, not by test setup.
Where invalid input could mutate state, the test asserts no protected side effect occurred.
verifier_detail: Identify input-validation tests by URN kind segment `-INPUT-`, `-VALIDATION-` or `-VALIDATE-`; only these tests are scanned.
Rejection signals: `.rejects`, `toThrow`, 400, 422, `invalid`, `reject`, or an error expectation. Any one of the listed signals satisfies the rule.
Detector: identifies input-validation tests from the URN and flags those with no rejection assertion (implementation: validator bun_tester_discipline_detector).
audit: schema_version 1.1.0; kind rule; status active; introduced_in 0.1.0.

splitSuggestion.then: When accepting invalid input could create or mutate state, the input-validation test MUST assert the rejected request left the protected effect absent.

additions.text: The conditional no-protected-side-effect assertion (S018/S026) is an independent obligation; kept in prefer/evidence here and proposed as tester.bun.security-input-no-side-effect.

additions.justification: Required by output schema; derived only from the source scanning scope (URN kind segment) and rejection signals, with no phase or changed-file restriction. Fires examples are restricted to the mechanical absence-of-any-signal trigger.

additions.text: Parenthetical noting the detector may not flag unrelated-error rejections.
additions.justification: Clarifies that this anti-pattern is normative guidance, not a detector finding, consistent with the any-signal exception (S038).

trace.note: Scope boundary expressed as activation (URN kind segment only; no phase or changed-test restriction), not a waiver.
Any listed signal satisfies the detector; fires examples only cover absence of all signals.
Kept as the bare source value 'strict'; no extra disposition semantics added.
